cards.text: Jesus has been drawing crowds, and now some visitors show up: Pharisees and scribes, religious leaders and teachers of the law, who came all the way from Jerusalem. They've got a question for Jesus about His disciples. Friend, when people travel that far just to ask you one question, it is NOT a compliment question.

cards.question: The Pharisees and scribes say Jesus' disciples break the tradition of the elders. What are the disciples doing?

answers.text: They don't wash their hands before they eat
They don't fast twice a week like others
They don't pray three times every day

cards.text: Hand washing. That's what they came all the way from Jerusalem to bring up. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer under the dust, and NOBODY ever made a trip to check my hands.

cards.question: The Pharisees and scribes asked why the disciples break the tradition of the elders. Jesus answers with a question of His own. What does He ask them?

answers.text: Why they break God's command for their tradition
Why they came all this way to ask about hands
Why they never wash their own hands either

cards.text: Then Jesus goes straight to what God said: 'Honor your father and mother.' And the other half: 'Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death.'

But Jesus says their teaching goes another way. If someone tells his father or mother, 'Whatever you would have received from me is a gift devoted to God,' then their tradition says something about him.

cards.question: In the Pharisees' teaching, a man tells his parents his money is a gift devoted to God. What does their tradition say happens then?

answers.text: He doesn't have to honor his parents with it
He must bring it to the temple that same day
He has to split it evenly with his parents

cards.question: Jesus sums up what their tradition does: "Thus you ___ the word of God for the sake of your ___."

cards.text: Then Jesus doesn't soften it one bit: 'You hypocrites!' They came to talk about hands, and now THEY'RE the ones getting looked at.

cards.question: Jesus says one of Israel's prophets prophesied correctly about these Pharisees and scribes. Which prophet?

cards.text: Isaiah was one of Israel's prophets, and Jesus says Isaiah got these leaders right. Isaiah's words are about two things: lips and hearts.

cards.question: In the words from Isaiah that Jesus quotes, these people honor God with their lips. Where are their hearts?
In the words from Isaiah that Jesus quotes, God says the worship of these people is worth a lot to Him. True or false?

cards.text: God says, 'They worship Me in vain; they teach as doctrine the precepts of men.' Nice words on the outside, far away on the inside: that was me in the drawer, telling the dead batteries I shared it with 'I'm FINE' with dust up to my eyebrows.
Then Jesus calls the crowd to Him and says, 'Listen and understand.' Friend, that's TWO jobs. On a good day I'm good for one.

cards.question: Jesus tells the crowd what really defiles a man. What does He say defiles him?

answers.text: What comes out of his mouth

cards.text: Then the disciples come to Jesus with an update about the Pharisees.

cards.question: The disciples tell Jesus the Pharisees were pleased when they heard His teaching about what defiles a man. True or false?

cards.text: The disciples ask, 'Are You aware that the Pharisees were offended when they heard this?' I bet they said it like somebody leaning over to tell you the boss is in a MOOD.
Jesus answers with a picture: 'Every plant that My heavenly Father has not planted will be pulled up by its roots.'

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples to disregard the Pharisees. What does He call them?
Jesus says if a blind man leads a blind man, what happens to them?

cards.text: Two blind men, one pit. It's like following a driver who has NO idea where he's going: different cars, SAME ditch.
Then Peter, one of Jesus' disciples, says, 'Explain this parable to us.'

cards.question: Peter asks Jesus to explain the parable. Before explaining, Jesus asks the disciples a question. What does He ask?

answers.text: Why they told Him about the Pharisees
If the crowd had understood it

cards.text: Jesus asks, 'Do you still not understand?' I bet Peter just asked what everybody was thinking, and I respect it, because I have been THAT guy in every meeting.

cards.question: Jesus explains the first half of the parable. According to Jesus, where does whatever enters the mouth go?

answers.text: Into the stomach and then out
Into the heart and stays there
Into the mind and changes it

cards.question: Jesus says the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart, and these things defile a man. True or false?
Jesus names what comes out of the heart. Which of these is on His list?

cards.text: Here's the whole list Jesus gives: evil thoughts, murder, adultery, sexual immorality, theft, false testimony and slander. Not one thing on that list ever came off a dirty hand.

cards.question: Jesus brings it back to where it started: "These are what defile a man, but eating with ___ hands does not defile him."

cards.text: So the unwashed hands the Pharisees and scribes came from Jerusalem to ask about don't defile a man. Jesus says what defiles a man comes out of the heart.
